title: Ventricular fibrillation in cardiac arrest
الرجفان البطيني أثناء توقف القلب
vignette: A patient is unresponsive with no palpable pulse. This rhythm is on the monitor.

options: Yes - ventricular fibrillation is shockable; defibrillate immediately per the arrest algorithm
No - this rhythm never requires defibrillation
Only if the patient also has a pulse
Yes, but only after giving amiodarone first
question.explanation: Ventricular fibrillation is one of the two shockable cardiac-arrest rhythms (with pulseless VT). Defibrillation should not be delayed - it is given as soon as the rhythm is identified and the defibrillator is ready, per the resuscitation algorithm.

title: Pulseless ventricular tachycardia
تسرع النظم البطيني بلا نبض
vignette: A patient is unresponsive with no palpable pulse. This rhythm is on the monitor.

options: Yes - pulseless ventricular tachycardia is shockable, just like ventricular fibrillation
No - ventricular tachycardia is never shockable
Only if it has been present for more than 5 minutes
No - this requires CPR only, never defibrillation
question.explanation: A regular, wide-complex tachycardia with no pulse is pulseless VT - the second shockable arrest rhythm alongside VF. It is treated the same way: defibrillate without delay per the arrest algorithm.

title: Asystole
توقف القلب (آسيستول)
vignette: A patient is unresponsive with no palpable pulse. This rhythm is on the monitor, and leads/connections have been confirmed.

options: No - asystole is a non-shockable rhythm; continue high-quality CPR and follow the non-shockable arm of the algorithm
Only if it persists for over a minute
Yes, but at a lower energy setting
question.explanation: Asystole (flat line, with leads/connections confirmed) is non-shockable - a defibrillator cannot organise electrical activity that is not there. The priority is high-quality, uninterrupted CPR and following the non-shockable arm of the resuscitation algorithm.

title: Pulseless electrical activity (PEA)
النشاط الكهربائي بلا نبض
vignette: A patient is unresponsive with no palpable pulse, despite this organised-looking rhythm on the monitor.

options: No - an organised rhythm with no pulse is PEA, a non-shockable rhythm; continue CPR and search for a reversible cause
Yes - any rhythm without a pulse should be shocked
Yes - this is actually ventricular fibrillation
No action is needed if the monitor shows an organised rhythm
question.explanation: An organised-looking rhythm (even one that looks like a normal sinus rhythm) with no palpable pulse is pulseless electrical activity (PEA) - non-shockable. The priority is high-quality CPR and searching for a reversible cause, not defibrillation; a monitor showing an organised rhythm never substitutes for checking the pulse.
